mechaber.en:
Time for sounding the shofar, and regarding this there are 5 paragraphs. The
time to sound the shofar is during the day, and not at night. The mitzvah is [binding] from the sunrise [netz hachamah, the sun is visible in the horizon] onwards. And if one sounded since dawn [when the sun has began to illuminate but is not yet visible] one has fulfilled the obligation. However, if one heard the shofar being sounded partly before dawn and partly after dawn, one has not fulfilled one's obligation.And if there was the shiur (minimal halachic amount) of tekiah blasts in that what he heard in the day, see what was explained in Siman 597 Paragraph 3.

וידמה לו שהוא יום ויהיה עדיין לילה לכך עשו לו זמן קבוע לנץ החמה דא"א לטעות. ולפי"ז י"ל דמשום חשש ברכה לבטלה לא היו מתקנין דס"ל כדעת התוס' דכל דרך ברכה הוי רק דרבנן והוי ספק דרבנן רק בשביל חשש ביטול גוף המצוה תקנו כן ומגילה נמי כיון דהוי ד"ק כד"ת דמיא וספיקו להחמיר יש לו' דדוקא גבי מגילה ומילה והזאה וטבילה דאין דרך לעשותו כן כמה פעמים ביום אחד דמילה א"א וכן הזאה יחזור ויטמא בהזאה שניה וכן טבילה (ג) לא יצא - דסוף תקיעה בלא תחלה לא מהני ולא מידי וכדלעיל בסימן תקפ"ז ס"ג [וה"ה אם שמע מקצת תקיעה ביום ומקצתה אח"כ בלילה ג"כ לא יצא דתחלה בלא סוף ג"כ לא מהני ולא מידי וכנ"ל שם] ונראה דאפילו היום שנוהגין לתקוע ל' קולות לצאת ידי כל ספק צריכין ג"כ ליזהר שאף תקיעה ראשונה לא תהיה אפילו מקצתה קודם אור היום:
(ד) נתבאר בסימן תקפ"ז ס"ג - ולפי מה שכתבנו שם דהעיקר כדעה א' א"כ בכל גווני לא יצא:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(1) By day and not by night - For it is written, "a day of teruah it shall be for you." If it extends until twilight, he should blow without a berachah.
(2) He has fulfilled - By strict law, from alot hashachar it is day for all matters. But because not everyone is expert in identifying it, and at times one may come to do it too early, the Sages required lechatchilah to wait until sunrise, which is clear day for everyone. It is not necessary to wait until the entire body of the sun has risen over the earth; from the beginning of sunrise it is also permitted lechatchilah, as Peri Megadim writes. However, all this is from the basic Torah law, or in pressing circumstances such as when he must set out on a journey and the like. But the Sages established shofar blowing during Mussaf, and the Gemara explains that in a time of decree they would not allow Israel to blow the shofar and would lie in wait for them during all six hours of the Shacharit time; therefore they moved it to Mussaf. For this reason it appears that all Israel have practiced from ancient times, even regarding the seated blasts, not to be among the eager who hurry and blow at the beginning of the day, but rather near Mussaf after Torah reading. Even an individual blowing for himself should also be careful to blow after roughly three hours, so that his blowing occurs when the congregation is engaged in blowing.
(3) He has not fulfilled - For the end of a blast without its beginning is of no effect at all, as above in siman 587 seif 3. The same applies if he heard part of a blast by day and part afterward at night: he has not fulfilled, for a beginning without an end is also of no effect, as above there. It appears that even today, when the practice is to blow thirty sounds to satisfy every doubt, one must also be careful that even the first tekiah should not have any part before daylight.
(4) It was explained in siman 587 seif 3 - According to what we wrote there, that the main view is the first opinion, in every case he has not fulfilled.

rabbi_akiva_eiger.en: Maga Skag here does not complicate anything. The main difference of the dress is not whether it comes out by sticking or it comes out by hearing it. The dam stops with the act that cheers a second cheer, cheers, and really if the other hearer who heard cheers cheered, he cheers, because he stopped in the act. But he heard a second cheer for the sake of a mitzvah, but he did not stop because he did not take action. And really, even if the other player gave a second cheer for a mitzvah, he wouldn't stop. And yet there is no evidence from Rabbi Dashfir, the rabbinate means 9 takkiot, even if the hearer made a decision in the act of speaking and the like, then he made a decision in the act of speaking, and the like, so he made a decision in the act, and again there is no division between a knock and a hearer, and the rabbi had to divide between a takiya and a faded ruling.

chokhmat_shlomo.en: (There seif 3) He heard nine tekios from nine people who all blew as one — he did not fulfill etc. NB: here there are variant readings in the Gemara — some read fulfilled and some read did not fulfill; and in my opinion the main reading is like this reading did not fulfill, as Shulchan Aruch wrote, and it is compelled in the Gemara from what we read there in tractate Rosh Hashanah daf 34: R' Yochanan said: one who heard nine tekios from nine people in nine hours of the day fulfilled etc.; and who said R' Yochanan thus, for R' Yochanan said in Hallel and Megillah: once he waited time to finish all of it he returns to the beginning etc.; and it is very difficult for me why he challenges those who hold [Shulchan Aruch Laws of Kriat Shema siman 64] that waiting time to finish all of it returning to beginning is only when he waited due to coercion, but without coercion he does not return — if so why does he challenge, perhaps R' Yochanan deals with interruption not due to coercion, therefore he fulfilled; and this view is greatly astonishing and I have not seen one who noticed this; therefore it appears to answer thus: the reason of the view that distinguishes between waiting due to coercion or not must be the reason that it is like what we establish: whatever is fit for kneading, kneading does not prevent it; and what is not fit for kneading, kneading prevents it — so too here if not due to coercion and fit to be together, therefore even though not together it helps; but where due to coercion and not fit for kneading, kneading prevents it, therefore it fits well there; but in tekios, since he heard nine tekios from nine people as one, he did not fulfill because there is no plain tekiah before it and plain tekiah after it; and why should we not say behold it is fit for kneading and fit for listeners one after another — this proves that regarding plain before and plain after, fit for kneading does not help, only we require literally before him and after him; and if so here too if there is interruption of another matter this is not at all before and after, only per those who say waiting time to finish all does not return, even when due to coercion it is not fit for kneading per force for him waiting is not considered interruption by itself, therefore it is also considered before and after; but per those who say waiting time to finish all returns to beginning, per force this is considered interruption, therefore where not due to coercion it is not interruption, i.e. from another reason it is fit for kneading; but if so in tekios since he heard from nine people as one he did not fulfill, for we require before and after and behold it is fit for kneading; and per force that regarding before and after fit for kneading does not help and we require before and after literally; therefore where there is interruption it is not before and after literally and fit for kneading does not help here; and he challenges well; therefore the matters compel that we read here did not fulfill — for if the reading were fulfilled, our difficulty stands in its place, why does he challenge; therefore in any case for those who hold there specifically due to coercion he did not fulfill, this reading is also compelled; even for those who hold in any case he did not fulfill, nevertheless our difficulty stands, since the Gemara wishes to prove from this that in any case waiting does not return — and if so whence do we know this, perhaps in truth there is a distinction between where fit for kneading or not as we establish in several places, and we can say what R' Yochanan said that he returns is where not entirely possible, but where possible he does not return — and why does he challenge; and per force as said; and it is proven this reading is primary; and study well, for it is a great proof with God's help; and see my works on Orach Chayim year 5601 daf 6a in siman 587 seif 5 what he wrote on this — see there and study well;
